clue.text: Slapdash meals you won't get out here

definitions.text: Slapdash meals you won't get out here

parts.words: Slapdash meals you won't get out here
parts.note: slapdash food is fare that is not thorough; run together, that phrase names the sign on a road with no way through, where you cannot get out the far end

explanation.surface: A diner warns that the hurried cooking means you will never eat out here.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun runs NOT THOROUGH and FARE together, sharing a T; the real sense is the road sign for a dead end.
explanation.definitionFit: The sign marks a road or passage that offers no through route, so a traveller cannot leave by the other end.

clue.text: Expert's taken past Gilbert White's study

parts.note: a natural is someone with an inborn gift, an expert
history is the past

explanation.surface: A specialist has been taken through the eighteenth-century naturalist's past.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert White was an 18th-century English parson famous for The Natural History of Selborne; 'taken' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: White's famous book records his observations of wildlife, the field of study described by this two-word phrase.

clue.text: Top out of everyone in the exam

indicators.note: the word for everyone is placed inside the word for the exam

parts.note: a test is an exam
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A pupil comes top of the whole class in the examination.
explanation.definitionFit: To top a group in height is to be the highest of them, the superlative of being high.

clue.text: Periods of play in which Wanderers can't get started

indicators.note: the word for wanderers loses its opening letter, as if unable to begin

parts.note: rovers are wanderers

explanation.surface: A football club called Wanderers keeps failing to get going in some phases of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket play is divided into these sets of six deliveries, each a period of play.

clue.text: Travel measure one may need to work in remote resort

indicators.note: the word for work is placed inside the rearranged letters
to re-sort is to sort again, so the letters of remote are rearranged

parts.note: to do is to work

explanation.surface: A traveller in a far-flung holiday spot needs a gadget to measure distance for work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday destination but is the anagram signal, read as re-sort; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's mileage meter records distance travelled, a measure a driver may need.

clue.text: Contracts about riding and styles of dress required

indicators.note: the word for contracts goes around the word for riding

parts.note: to contract an illness is to get it, so contracts means gets
a jockey who is riding is said to be up

explanation.surface: A dress code for equestrian events is written into the agreements.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit, especially an elaborate or odd one, is informally a costume of this kind.

clue.text: Do without after tax rises are overlooked

parts.note: to forgo is to do without

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a nett sum is what remains after tax

explanation.surface: Going without once taxes climb is something people simply ignore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns NETT upwards to TTEN; 'are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overlooked has slipped from memory or attention, a synonym.

clue.text: Gunners on plateau liable to be charged

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
a table, or tableland, is a plateau

explanation.surface: Artillerymen camped on a high plain may find themselves charged by the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: Property that is rateable is assessed for local tax, so liable to be charged.

clue.text: Handicapped pirate only able to take coins one at a time

definitions.text: only able to take coins one at a time
definitions.meaning: a slot machine whose slot accepts a single coin per pull

explanation.walkthrough: The slot machine is nicknamed for its single lever and its habit of robbing players.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname for a fruit machine pictures a thief with one arm, its single lever.

clue.text: Blocked bill, having nothing left to say

definitions.meaning: a parliamentary bill killed by filibustering until time runs out
exhausted by speaking, all words used up

explanation.walkthrough: In Parliament a bill is filibustered to death when debate runs on until its time expires.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from prolonged speech: one ends a bill, the other leaves a speaker drained.

clue.text: Artist with brown walking-stick

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: A painter goes about with a brown cane.
explanation.walkthrough: RATAN is a variant spelling of rattan, a cane made from palm stems.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattan canes are cut from climbing palms and used as walking sticks.

clue.text: King explosive because these birds won't fly

parts.note: R is short for Rex, king
HE is high explosive
as means because

explanation.surface: A monarch is furious because some birds refuse to take off.
explanation.definitionFit: These large South American ratites are flightless runners, like small ostriches.

clue.text: Feeling happy about first sign of bracts in the poinsettia

indicators.note: the word for feeling happy wraps around the letter

parts.note: euphoria is a feeling of great happiness

indicators.note: only the opening letter of bracts is used

explanation.surface: A gardener is delighted by the coloured leaves on a Christmas plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link: the poinsettia belongs to the spurge genus.
explanation.definitionFit: The poinsettia is a species of spurge, the genus whose Latin name this is.

clue.text: Stretcher man provided bedding

parts.note: a litter is a stretcher for carrying the sick
Ed is a man's name

explanation.surface: A stretcher-bearer supplied mattresses for the wounded.
explanation.definitionFit: Litter is straw laid for animals to sleep on, so to litter a stall is to give it bedding.

clue.text: Like a puzzle? Changes get one manic

indicators.note: used as a verb, changes alters the letters that follow

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A solver asks whether constant alterations to a puzzle drive people mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes' shuffles GET, I and MANIC together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something baffling and mysterious is puzzling, so it is like a riddle.

clue.text: The way many papers display class division

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
a ream is a large quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: Newspapers lay out the divisions between social classes in their own manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'display' is a link. British schools stream pupils, grouping them into classes by ability.
explanation.definitionFit: A school stream is a division of a year group into classes by ability.

clue.text: He is employed provisionally in college hall

definitions.text: He is employed provisionally in college hall

parts.words: He is employed provisionally in college hall
parts.note: provisionally seems to mean temporarily but here means in charge of provisions, as a steward buying food for a college

explanation.surface: A temporary worker has been taken on in a university dining room.
explanation.walkthrough: The old title survives at some Oxford and Cambridge colleges, and in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales.
explanation.definitionFit: This officer buys food and provisions for a college or inn of court.

clue.text: Damage — I am needing a brace

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
a brace is a pair

explanation.surface: Someone with a hurt back says they need a support.
explanation.walkthrough: A brace of game birds is two, a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To weaken or harm something is to damage it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Old ruler of troubled Arapaho lost a husband

indicators.note: troubled letters are stirred up and rearranged
one A goes from the tribe's name and is replaced

explanation.surface: A troubled Native American widow mourns her lost husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost a' swaps one A of ARAPAHO for H, giving RAPAHOH, which 'troubled' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An Egyptian king of antiquity bore this title, so an old ruler.

clue.text: Denied successes needed help

parts.note: gains are successes
aid is help

explanation.surface: Someone refused advancement because the help they needed was withheld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to contradict or deny, so the past tense means denied.

clue.text: Wind English find harsh

parts.note: Auster is the south wind

explanation.surface: English people find the cold wind severe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An austere manner or regime is severe and stern, a synonym of harsh.

clue.text: Difficult position of Gibraltar, for example

definitions.meaning: a narrow sea channel between two landmasses

explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a predicament; the other is a narrow channel like that off southern Spain.

clue.text: Disposing of Marat with one cut was shocking

indicators.note: to dispose letters is to arrange them, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: The killing of the revolutionary Marat with a knife was appalling.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean-Paul Marat was stabbed in his bath in 1793; 'with' and 'was' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A traumatic event causes deep psychological shock, so it is shocking.

clue.text: Stabbed by him, Caesar falls? Not altogether

indicators.note: the word for falls is not given in full, its end cut off

parts.note: cascades are waterfalls

explanation.surface: Caesar collapses after being stabbed, though not dead entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Julius Caesar, Casca strikes the first blow before the dying line 'Then fall, Caesar'.
explanation.definitionFit: Casca was one of the conspirators, and the first to stab Julius Caesar.

clue.text: About to warm up in fleece

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
to heat is to warm up

explanation.surface: Someone warms up wearing a fleece jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to swindle them, which is to cheat them.

clue.text: Severely criticise most of Sartor Resartus

indicators.note: Latin for patched up again, so the letters are reworked
the word loses its final letter, leaving most of it

explanation.surface: A critic is asked to savage Carlyle's book Sartor Resartus.
explanation.walkthrough: Sartor Resartus, Carlyle's novel, means 'the tailor re-tailored'; 'Resartus' rearranges SARTO.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast someone is to criticise or ridicule them harshly.

clue.text: Fear arrest

definitions.meaning: to seize and detain a suspect

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to anticipate with dread and to take a suspect into custody.

clue.text: What Delilah gave Sampson was a nasty surprise

definitions.meaning: she had his hair cut, so his shock of hair was dealt with
a sudden jolt, figuratively electroconvulsive therapy

explanation.walkthrough: A shock is a mass of hair; Samson's strength lay in his hair, which Delilah had cut. 'was' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names harsh therapy and, by extension, any brutal jolt; a shock of hair is a thick mop.
